subject: Privilege scope questions and rollback schedule for proposed subprocessor change
messages:
From: Maya Greene <maya.greene@acmepayments.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: subprocessor privileges & rollback ask

Hi Olga,

Hope you're well. We're reviewing the proposed subprocessor change you flagged yesterday and our security team has a couple of focused questions we need answered before procurement will greenlight the change:

- Which subprocessors will have any ability to access encryption material or KMS-related metadata (even if only for key rotation/ops)? Please list roles and the exact breadth of privilege (e.g., rotate-only, exportable, emergency-unseal).
- If Redwood executes a subprocessor swap, what is the rollback/mitigation schedule you can commit to (timeline and steps) in the event the new processor causes regression or exposes data path differences?

We understand some details are sensitive — redacted export of the KMS matrix would be fine. Can you get us an initial reply within 48 hours? We also may request a short call if there are non‑standard controls.

Thanks,
Maya Greene
InfoSec Lead, Acme Payments
security@acmepayments.com

P.S. Procurement copied for awareness. Attachment: sample-ask-template.xlsx (we filled in our expected fields)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maya Greene <maya.greene@acmepayments.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor privileges & rollback ask

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the fast turnaround from your side.

Short answer up front: we can provide a redacted KMS/access matrix, commit to a documented rollback playbook with target timelines, and propose a 30‑day notification window for non-emergency subprocessor swaps (emergency operational swaps will follow the playbook with faster notice where possible).

What I'll do now:
- Attach a current subprocessor manifest PDF (redwood-subprocessor-manifest-20270707.pdf) with roles mapped to privilege classes.
- Attach a redacted KMS access CSV (kms-access-matrix-redacted.csv) showing rotate vs. export vs. emergency-unseal flags.
- Loop in Legal/Procurement so we can surface any DPA addendum language (kimberly_park) and confirm commercial timelines (connor_obrien).

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send the redacted artifacts now (see attachments).
2) Kimberly, Connor — can Legal/Procurement review the DPA/notification wording and propose a draft addendum? If possible, please aim for a draft within 48 hours so Acme can review.
3) Maya — if you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the manifest and the rollback playbook.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-manifest-20270707.pdf; kms-access-matrix-redacted.csv
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maya Greene <maya.greene@acmepayments.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor privileges & rollback ask

On Thu, Jul 7, 2027 at 9:34 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed next steps:
> 1) I will send the redacted artifacts now (see attachments).

Thanks, Olga and Maya — looping Legal and Customer Success for transparency.

From a DPA perspective, Redwood can commit to the following items that address your two asks:
- Privilege disclosure: Provide a redacted KMS/access matrix that identifies roles assigned to subprocessors and the scope of any crypto operations (rotate-only, seal/unseal, export). We'll include a short legend for clarity.
- Rollback/playbook: We will supply a rollback playbook that includes an expected mitigation timeline (initial detection to revert target: typically 6–24 hours for operational rollback steps, full validation window up to 72 hours depending on data volumes) plus a communication template for customers and a canary run plan.
- Notification window: Standard non-emergency changes — 30 days notice. Emergency operational swaps (security/availability) — we'll provide as‑soon‑as‑possible notification and follow the rollback playbook.

I'll attach a DPA addendum draft for your review (dpa_addendum_draft.docx). Two quick asks for your team:
1) Please confirm if Acme needs logging-at-rest evidence for any new subprocessor prior to approval.
2) If you require contractual language around KMS custody, flag specific clauses so we can tailor the addendum.

Grace (CS lead) — can you confirm the customer‑facing canary schedule we typically use for similar customers (30‑minute rolling canary, metrics baseline, rollback trigger thresholds)?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Attachments: dpa_addendum_draft.docx
From: Maya Greene <maya.greene@acmepayments.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jul 2027 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor privileges & rollback ask

Thanks — very helpful and timely. We'll review the manifest and the draft addendum today. A couple of quick points:

- Logging evidence: yes, please include recent attestations (logs showing role assignments and a sample key rotation event) if available — redacted is fine.
- Canary: the proposed canary plan sounds reasonable; we'll want the ability to extend the validation window if we see anomalies.

Would appreciate a 30‑minute call Friday morning to walk through the manifest and the addendum with your Legal and CS. If that works for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the quick attention.

Best,
Maya Greene
InfoSec Lead, Acme Payments
Maya.greene@acmepayments.com
